newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber end sharply mixed, new highs in nearbys.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber end sharply mixed, new highs in nearbys.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed sharply mixed with nearby November and January posting new contract highs on continued effects of the Canadian export quota on softwood lumber and sharply rising cash prices.

November paced the advance during the day and set a new high of $481.80 per thousand board feet before closing at $480.00, up $11.90 per tbf. January set a new high of $427.40 and then closed up $6.00 at $425.40 while other months finished $4.50 to $8.20 per tbf lower.
Nearbys found strong carryover support from the recent sharp advance in lumber prices.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $468 per tbf Wednesday morning, up $42 per tbf since last Friday. Private reports later put mill asking prices as high as $485 per tbf.
"Most of the higher mill asking prices are coming from uncertainty over the effects of the recently announced individual (company) export quotas" on softwood lumber from Canada, one trader said.
Deferred months were pressured by ideas lumber availability will increase at the start of a new quota year next spring, traders added.
